newsitem.title: USA: AMR says USAir lawsuit without merit.
newsitem.headline: AMR says USAir lawsuit without merit.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said on Friday that USAir Group Inc's lawsuit against American was without merit.
USAir, which is partially owned by British Airways Plc, sued British Airways and American Airlines over their plans to form a marketing alliance because it violated a previous agreement.
American said in a statement it had asked a federal judge to dismiss the lawsuit.
The proposed alliance, announced on July 11 , was subject to U.S. and U.K. government approval and liberalization of the aviation treaty between the two governments, American said in a statement.
USAir alleged the alliance violated a 1993 non-exclusive marketing agreement it formed with British Airways, American said.
The deal was part of a larger transaction in which British Airways invested over $300 million in USAir, American said.
USAir was not immediately available to comment on American's motion.
American said USAir's claims were "unwarranted and unfounded."

"USAir's lawsuit reflects USAir's frustration with their British Airways agreement," Senior Vice President and General Counsel Anne McNamara said. "While we're sorry that they're unhappy, that doesn't mean we did anything wrong."
McNamara rejected USAir's claims that the proposed alliance violated U.S. antitrust laws.
"We have said from the beginning that our alliance won't go forward unless we are granted antitrust immunity from our government, so suing us for anti-trust violations is just plain silly."
